cases.description: Microsoft's example: an annuity's present value
With a future value, at the start of each period
A type of 2 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-008 found it is for PMT
A number of periods that is not a whole number: 1+rate is raised to it as e^(nper ln(1+rate)), which gives Excel's double; a correctly rounded power is two units in the last place away
Where dividing by the growth and multiplying by its reciprocal, and the order of the payment's factors, differ in the last place (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/): Excel's double is the engine's

At the start of each period: the payment multiplies (1+rate)*((g-1)/rate), Excel's grouping; multiplying the payment by 1+rate first is one unit in the last place below Excel's (spikes/exsheet-financial-evaluation/)
A type of 0.5 is payment at the start of each period, as PMT-009 found it is for PMT
A negative number of periods: 1 over 1+rate raised by squaring, as FV-007's
Half a period: the square root of 1+rate, as FV-016's; e^(0.5 ln(1+rate)) gives the same double here (PV-014 is where they part)
Half a period at a rate below -1: a negative 1+rate has no square root, and PV is #NUM!; a fraction whose reciprocal is odd has an odd root (FV-017)
Ten periods before, at a rate of -1: 0 to a negative power is #DIV/0!, as FV-021's is

Refused until Excel is asked: at a rate of -1 the growth is 0 to the power 10, 0, and PV divides by it; which Error Value Excel gives there has not been observed (FV-018's #NUM! and FV-020's #DIV/0! come from the power, not from a division)

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: half a period is the square root of 1+rate, as FV-016's, PV raising 1+rate as FV does (PV-005 and PV-009 to PV-012 agree); e^(0.5 ln(1+rate)) gives 38.29015278650262
Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: 1 over the power to 2.5, as FV-022's; raising to -2.5 directly gives -250.9382807624435

Engine's answer, Excel to be asked: e^(nper ln(1+rate)) with the exponential and the logarithm correctly rounded, the engine's, gives 1091.2943662943903; glibc's exp and log, which .NET takes on Linux, give 1091.2943662943944. XNPV-013 found Excel's exponential correctly rounded where glibc's is not; no observed double tells the logarithms apart
